articles.title: 5 men arrested near UK air base used by US in Iran war on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
articles.summary: U.K. police said that five men arrested in the early hours of Sunday near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — U.K. police said that five men arrested in the early hours of Sunday near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran are being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act that appeared to involve three trucks.

London's Metropolitan Police, which takes the lead on potential terrorist activities, said police received a call at 12:45 a.m. related to the three suspicious vehicles that appeared to be traveling toward RAF Fairford, a U.K.-owned base that is operated by the U.S. under an agreement dating back to the Cold War.

The base is home to US bombers striking Iran

The arrests come at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states to the U.K., with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil. In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states including Iran increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.

Fairford has been used by American bombers for strictly limited strikes against Iranian missile sites under an agreement with former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who voiced opposition to the war after it was launched by the U.S. and Israel on Feb. 28.

Authorities are investigating a link between the Fairford arrests and Iran as one possibility. Iran has previously indicated that a base used to attack its territory is a legitimate target .

U.S. President Donald Trump praised those who were involved in making the arrests.

"It was an amazing job. We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort. And working with the British worked out great," he told reporters in Chicago on Sunday. "We had them under view for a long time and we got them."

The five men were initially arrested on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act in the Whelford area, which backs onto RAF Fairford, which hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and the 420th Air Base Squadron.

Aerial footage from Sky News appeared to show a bomb disposal robot roaming between three white trucks. The rear doors of two of the vans were open and large black items could be seen scattered around. The robot appeared to be working toward getting access to the third truck.

Police gave no details as to the nationality of those arrested. Suspects arrested under the Terrorism Act 2000 can be detained for up to 14 days without charge, compared to the 24-hour limit for standard arrests, without an extension application.

"We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody," said Vicki Evans, the Met's counterterrorism policing senior national coordinator.

Evans said a 400-meter (yard) cordon has been put in place around the three vehicles that raised suspicion while the army conducts examinations. As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place. Some have been taken to a nearby recreation center.

The U.S. embassy in London warned Americans to be cautious and mindful of their personal security.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he knew the incident would be "deeply concerning" for many. In a post on social media, Burnham thanked police and the armed forces for their response and said he was grateful to the residents who have been evacuated from their homes "while precautionary checks are carried out."

He urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts."

The defense secretaries of the U.S. and the U.K., Pete Hegseth and Wes Streeting, have also spoken about the incident.

British security officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson and sabotage attempts in the U.K. and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

Local residents evacuated as investigation continues

Gloucestershire police said the situation appeared to be "contained" and urged residents to follow official advice while the investigation continues.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said another resident had reported seeing three "suspicious vans" in the village early on Sunday.

"There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there's been a major incident, said he couldn't elaborate," he said.

Associated Press writers Jill Lawless in Liverpool, England, and Ben Finley in Washington, D.C. contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ronaldo Caiado, candidato do PSD à Presidência, faz campanha em Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato falou sobre projetos na área de segurança pública e defendeu a redução da maioridade penal.
articles.summary: Candidato falou sobre projetos na área de segurança pública e defendeu a redução da maioridade penal.
articles.body:
O candidato Ronaldo Caiado , do PSD , ficou em Goiânia.

Pela manhã, Ronaldo Caiado participou de uma caminhada no bairro Jardim Guanabara, conhecido por abrigar o maior parque de indústrias moveleiras da cidade. Ele estava acompanhado do candidato ao governo de Goiás Daniel Vilela, do MDB. Caiado defendeu a redução dos gastos públicos para investir em áreas como saúde e educação.

O candidato também falou sobre projetos na área de segurança pública e defendeu a redução da maioridade penal:

“Você não pode imaginar que as pessoas com 16 anos de idade não tenham conhecimento da barbárie que ele está praticando. E, dentro daquilo que é a proposta de nós diminuirmos a idade, é dentro daqueles crimes que são verdadeiras aberrações”.

Esse foi o único compromisso público de Caiado nesta segunda-feira (28). Depois, ele foi para São Paulo, onde passou a tarde gravando programa eleitoral.

articles.title: Frente fria deve trazer chuva e rajadas de vento a partir desta terça | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança nas condições meteorológicas ocorre entre terça-feira (29) e quinta-feira (1º), com pancadas de chuva, possibilidade de granizo e queda nas temperaturas em várias regiões paulistas.
articles.summary: Uma frente fria se aproxima do estado de São Paulo e deve causar pancadas de chuva e rajadas de vento entre terça-feira (29) e quinta-feira (1º), segundo a Defesa Civil estadual.
articles.body:
Estado de São Paulo está em atenção para pancadas de chuva e rajadas de vento — Foto: Defesa Civil estadual

Uma frente fria se aproxima do estado de São Paulo e deve causar pancadas de chuva e rajadas de vento entre terça-feira (29) e quinta-feira (1º), segundo alerta da Defesa Civil estadual.

Conforme o órgão, as chuvas poderão ser acompanhadas por raios, rajadas de vento e eventual queda isolada de granizo.

Na terça e na quarta-feira (30), as temperaturas ainda devem permanecer elevadas, mantendo a sensação de calor e abafamento. Com a aproximação da frente fria, aumenta a possibilidade de pancadas de chuva, que podem ser intensas em algumas regiões paulistas.

Na quinta-feira, a previsão é de chuva mais persistente, principalmente na faixa leste do estado de São Paulo. Após a passagem da frente fria, as temperaturas devem cair de forma mais acentuada, aumentando a sensação de frio em relação aos últimos dias.

A combinação de chuva e rajadas de vento pode provocar alagamentos, enxurradas, quedas de galhos e árvores, além de outros transtornos , principalmente em áreas mais vulneráveis.

Frente fria deve trazer chuva e rajadas de vento a partir desta terça-feira — Foto: Carla Monteiro/g1

Para reduzir os riscos e garantir a segurança da população, a Defesa Civil estadual recomenda:

Não atravessar áreas alagadas, vias, pontes ou córregos com acúmulo de água, a pé ou de veículo;

Durante raios e rajadas de vento, permanecer em local protegido, longe de árvores, postes, estruturas metálicas, torres e outras estruturas que possam oferecer risco.

Em caso de granizo, procurar abrigo e mantenha portas e janelas fechadas. Guarde veículos em locais cobertos;

Evitar a navegação e atividades náuticas;

Com a queda das temperaturas, manter crianças, idosos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade protegidos do frio.

Para receber gratuitamente os alertas da Defesa Civil por SMS, envie o CEP da localidade para o número 40199 .

Em situações de emergência, acione a Defesa Civil pelo 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 .

articles.title: Juliana Brizola destinar '30% da publicidade' para eventos climáticos | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.summary: Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.body:
Candidata ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PDT, Juliana Brizola cumpriu compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28). Ela esteve em Porto Alegre .

A ex-deputada participou de uma sabatina na Rádio Gaúcha, onde respondeu perguntas sobre saúde, educação e infraestrutura. A candidata promete acabar com as filas no SUS para consultas e exames e aumentar a fiscalização das parcerias público-privadas (PPPs).

Até o dia 2 de outubro, os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul vão responder perguntas feitas diretamente por eleitores entrevistados pela RBS TV. Serão seis temas, um a cada semana: segurança, saúde, educação, infraestrutura, economia e prevenção a desastres climáticos . Ao todo, 86 eleitores terão suas dúvidas respondidas .

Os candidatos terão 30 segundos para apresentar suas respostas. Dos sete candidatos, três responderão em cada dia . A ordem de aparição leva em conta a mais recente pesquisa eleitoral contratada pelo Grupo RBS , divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24).

Sobre prevenção a mudanças climáticas , a candidata escolheu a pergunta do eleitor Cláudio Reis, de Santa Cruz do Sul , no Vale do Rio Pardo. "Gostaria de saber qual é a proposta para esse sistema de alertas temporais no Rio Grande do Sul" , questiona.

"A população precisa de protocolos claros, de alertas que sejam transparentes, que sejam confiáveis. Eu vou destinar 30% da publicidade do nosso governo para orientar as pessoas com propagandas nos rádios, na televisão, na internet. Porque, infelizmente, hoje é um dia chuvoso, amanhã também, e as pessoas já estão com medo e não sabem o que fazer", afirmou Juliana.

articles.title: Mulher que ficou ferida em acidente com ônibus na BA será transferida  | G1
articles.standfirst: Graciele de Melo, de 23 anos, deve ser transportada em uma ambulância com UTI móvel. O corpo de Helena, de 2 anos, será velado na chácara da família, na zona rural de Palmas.
articles.summary: Graciele de Melo, de 23 anos, deve ser transportada em ambulância com UTI móvel. O corpo de Helena, de 2 anos será velado na chácara da família, na zona rural da capital.
articles.body:
Graciele de Melo Lima de Moraes, de 23 anos, que sobreviveu a um acidente com um ônibus na Bahia, será transferida para Palmas em uma ambulância com Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) móvel. Segundo o esposo dela, Jucinei Moraes, o velório da filha do casal, Helena Lima de Moraes, de 2 anos, que morreu no acidente, está previsto para esta terça-feira (29), na capital. A família é de Palmas.

Segundo nota da Secretaria de Segurança Pública da Bahia (SSP-BA), o acidente aconteceu na noite do dia 25, quando um ônibus da empresa Real Maia, que seguia de Fortaleza para Palmas, saiu da pista na BR-122, nas proximidades de Iraquara (BA). Conforme a empresa, 24 pessoas estavam no veículo, sendo 22 passageiros e dois motoristas. Sete morreram e 13 ficaram feridas.

Outras duas pessoas que estavam no ônibus também tinham o Tocantins como destino. O g1 tenta confirmar se elas estão entre os feridos no acidente.

A criança Helena viajava com a mãe, Graciele. De acordo com a família, mãe e filha retornavam para Palmas após uma viagem à casa da avó de Helena, em Pernambuco. Graciele sofreu fraturas nas pernas, além de fratura na bacia e lesão na coluna. Segundo o esposo, ela também será transferida para Palmas durante a madrugada desta terça-feira para continuar o tratamento.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Conforme Jucinei, a preparação do corpo da criança para o traslado foi concluída em Bonfinópolis (BA). O velório será realizado na residência da família, em uma chácara localizada no setor Santa Fé Rural, em Palmas.

Helena Lima ao lado da mãe antes de acidente em ônibus — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/ Elivonaldo de Melo Lima

Ônibus tombou na BR-122, em Iraquara, na Bahia. — Foto: Redes Sociais

A família buscava, desde o fim de semana, a transferência hospitalar para que a esposa pudesse passar por cirurgia e continuar a recuperação em Palmas. Ainda muito abalado, o pai contou sobre a dor de reconhecer o corpo da filha e o impacto da perda repentina.

"Eu estou conversando porque Deus está me fortalecendo. Uma criança de 2 anos e 2 meses... Para quem viu minha filha, o tanto que ela era bonitinha, eu não sei nem o que falar", desabafou.

A viação Real Maia informou, em nota inicial, que acionou a seguradora e presta assistência às vítimas e aos familiares. A empresa também se solidarizou com os familiares e amigos das vítimas.

articles.summary: Candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PSDB cumpriu compromissos de campanha em Porto Alegre.
articles.body:
Candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul pelo PSDB, Marcelo Maranata cumpriu compromissos de campanha nesta segunda-feira (28). Ele esteve em Porto Alegre .

O ex-prefeito de Guaíba cumpriu agenda no diretório do partido, no Centro Histórico de Porto Alegre. O candidato se reuniu com a equipe de campanha para ajustar detalhes de materiais de campanha que serão divulgados. Também discutiu destaques do plano de governo que pretende abordar no debate da RBS TV, que ocorre às 22h15 desta terça-feira (29) .

Até o dia 2 de outubro, os candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Sul vão responder perguntas feitas diretamente por eleitores entrevistados pela RBS TV. Serão seis temas, um a cada semana: segurança, saúde, educação, infraestrutura, economia e prevenção a desastres climáticos . Ao todo, 86 eleitores terão suas dúvidas respondidas .

Os candidatos terão 30 segundos para apresentar suas respostas. Dos sete candidatos, três responderão em cada dia . A ordem de aparição leva em conta a mais recente pesquisa eleitoral contratada pelo Grupo RBS , divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24).

Sobre prevenção a mudanças climáticas , o candidato escolheu a pergunta da eleitora Alana Maia, de Porto Alegre. "Candidato, qual a sua proposta para que as escolas consigam enfrentar as mudanças climáticas?" , questiona.

"Dentro da Defesa Civil, a gente vai ter um recurso especial para reconstruir escolas e postos de saúde o mais breve possível para a criança ter um lugar seguro. Mas também o ambiente da escola tem que ser o lugar que a gente vai debater todo o entorno da escola, evacuação e prevenção com relação aos problemas climáticos. Então, Alana, escola e saúde vão ser os primeiros lugares que a gente vai investir o dinheiro da Defesa Civil", afirmou Maranata.

articles.title: André Luís propõe incentivo ao microempreendedor e apoio a igrejas | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato ao governo do Maranhão pelo partido Missão falou sobre as propostas voltadas ao combate à pobreza e à ampliação da assistência social no estado.
articles.summary: O candidato ao governo do Maranhão pelo partido Missão falou sobre as propostas voltadas ao combate à pobreza e à ampliação da assistência social no estado.
articles.body:
O candidato ao Governo do Maranhão, André Luís ( Missão ), cumpriu agenda de campanha na manhã desta segunda-feira (28), em São Luís . O compromisso foi realizado na Feira da Cohab, onde conversou com eleitores e ouviu dos feirantes as principais demandas para melhorar as vendas e a estrutura do comércio.

Durante a visita, André Luís também apresentou propostas de governo para os próximos quatro anos e distribuiu material de campanha com foto e número para os eleitores.

O candidato falou ainda sobre propostas voltadas ao combate à pobreza e à ampliação da assistência social no Maranhão. Ele afirmou que pretende incentivar pequenos e microempreendedores, além de atrair empresas para o estado como forma de gerar emprego e renda. André Luís também defendeu o apoio do governo a igrejas e entidades religiosas que atuam em ações de assistência social.

"Combate à pobreza acontece quando se gera riqueza, o que gera riqueza é você quando incentivado pelo governo. Então, as medidas do nosso governo serão de apoio ao pequeno e microempreendedor, mas também à abertura do nosso estado, tirando as regras que vêm travando o desenvolvimento do nosso estado e atraindo empresas para se instalar aqui, gerando trabalho e renda para desenvolver os empregos e as oportunidades que nós precisamos para de fato combater a pobreza. E, no tocante à assistência social, nós precisamos lembrar do trabalho importantíssimo que as igrejas vêm fazer no nosso estado. Comunidades de fé vão onde o governo não alcança. É o braço do governo, é o braço do estado, cuidando das pessoas. E aqui na Cohab também é espaço onde tem muitos moradores de rua, usuários de droga, e o estado precisa apoiar essas entidades evangélicas que atuam nessa região", disse o candidato.

André Luís propõe incentivo ao microempreendedor e apoio a igrejas em ações de assistência social no MA — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

As eleições de 2026 serão realizadas em 4 de outubro , no primeiro turno. Caso seja necessário, o segundo turno ocorrerá em 25 de outubro para os cargos de presidente da República e governador.

Na votação, os eleitores escolherão candidatos aos cargos de deputado estadual, deputado federal, dois senadores, governador e presidente.

A campanha eleitoral segue até 3 de outubro , véspera do primeiro turno. Em caso de segundo turno, a propaganda será retomada e poderá ocorrer até 24 de outubro .

articles.summary: Four passengers were hospitalized for smoke inhalation after a Boston-bound Delta Air Lines flight made an emergency diversion to Porto, Portugal.
articles.body: A Boston-bound Delta Air Lines flight was forced to make an emergency landing in Portugal, disrupting travel plans for more than 280 passengers. The flight on Sunday from Barcelona, Spain, to Boston, Massachusetts, was diverted to Porto after smoke was detected in the cabin. Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported that 14 passengers required medical attention after the plane landed, citing Portugal's civil protection service. PROBE UNDERWAY AS 7 FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SICKENED BY BAFFLING ODOR ON MAJOR AIRLINE Of the 14 passengers, four were taken to local hospitals for smoke inhalation and were reportedly only "lightly" affected, the news agency said. A Delta spokesperson confirmed the Sept. 27 incident to Fox News Digital but did not comment on the hospitalization reports. The diversion was due to a "reported mechanical issue," the official said. "The flight landed safely, and we apologize to our customers for the delay in their travels as we work to get them to Boston as safely and quickly as possible," the spokesperson added. articles.title: New York Times executive fatally shot allegedly by elderly in-laws
articles.summary: Jonathan McKinsey's in-laws, who are both 77 years old, face multiple charges including first-degree murder.
articles.body:
A New York Times executive was fatally shot in California, allegedly by his wife's elderly parents who have been arrested on suspicion of murder.

Jonathan McKinsey, 40, the newspaper's director of engineering for games player experience, was found with multiple gunshot wounds in a car park in Dublin - 35 miles (56km) west of San Francisco - on Saturday afternoon, police said.

Shouyong Zhang and Shili Chen, his parents-in-law who are both 77 years old, are facing multiple charges, including first-degree murder.

It was unclear whether the couple have a lawyer, and they are due to appear in court to formally face the charges on Wednesday.

McKinsey's death was confirmed by The New York Times.

His body was found at 15:00 (23:00 GMT) on Thursday afternoon outside the Dublin Sports Grounds.

Witnesses told KGO-TV in San Francisco that they heard a flurry of gunshots, before seeing the victim on the ground.

"I saw the guy drop to the floor: head bloody and chest bloody," witness Assad Razawi told the news outlet.

His daughter added that her father saw the couple "walking together and then casually walk away from the shooting".

The couple were arrested several minutes later by an officer passing by the scene. They had remained in the area after the attack, a witness said.

McKinsey was pronounced dead at the scene, according to police.

Police have not disclosed any motive for his killing.

The elderly couple are being held at the Santa Rita jail.

They also face charges of felony conspiracy, wilful discharge of a firearm with gross negligence, and child endangerment.

articles.title: Ahead of rare execution, lone woman on Tennessee death row says ‘I am at peace’
articles.summary: Christa Pike, 50, was an accomplice in a murder she committed at 18. She would be the first woman executed by the state in over 200 years.
articles.body: With her execution days away, the lone woman on Tennessee’s death row says she is prepared to die but “nervous” about how the state intends to carry it out. Before learning Monday that Gov. Bill Lee would not be intervening in her case, Christa Pike wrote in a letter to NBC News, shared by her spiritual adviser: “Whether my clemency is granted or not, I am at peace.” “I am not afraid to die,” wrote Pike, who has been on death row for over three decades. “I’m only nervous about the process.” Tennessee is poised to execute Pike, 50, on Wednesday by lethal injection — the first time in more than 200 years that the state will put a woman to death, according to historical records. In 1995, Pike was 18 when Knoxville police say she and two teenage accomplices tortured, slashed and fatally beat Colleen Slemmer, 19. Police say Pike and the others lured Slemmer, a classmate in their Job Corps training program, to an abandoned steam plant at the nearby University of Tennessee and attacked her. The case became sensationalized when investigators said it was tied to the occult because someone had carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest and Pike bragged to another student that she had kept a fragment of the victim’s skull as a “souvenir.” Pike doesn’t dispute her role in the grisly killing. But details about her upbringing, marked by years of sexual and physical abuse and neglect, were not shared with the jury that sentenced her to death. Her lawyers believe that if such evidence of abuse were presented at a trial now, a death sentence would not be guaranteed. They have asked the Supreme Court to halt Pike’s execution, saying that she suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder stemming from being molested and raped beginning when she was a toddler. Being held down and strapped to a gurney, they wrote, will likely create “severe mental suffering and superadded psychological terror under Tennessee’s lethal injection protocol.” The state hasn’t denied that Pike has suffered from abuse. But in a response filed Monday, the attorney general’s office said a judge already concluded last month that it was “speculative whether Pike would suffer” greater mental harm from how the lethal injection protocol is carried out. The Supreme Court is Pike’s remaining chance for a reprieve after Lee said he was upholding her death sentence “after deliberate consideration.” Pike’s lawyers said Monday they were “saddened and heartbroken.” Another woman, Gaile Owens, was on Tennessee’s death row with Pike until 2010, when Gov. Phil Bredesen changed her sentence to life in prison. In her letter, Pike wrote that people have seen a “limited public persona that has been the only narrative” about her. Her lawyers had tried to convince Lee that she was a product of a tumultuous childhood. “Stepping into the chaos of Christa’s life that led her to that moment will not justify her actions that night,” one of her lawyers, Randall Spivey, said of when she committed her crime. “But the chaos will show you that Christa was broken, not evil.” Different sentences Pike’s lawyers also point to her age and how it led to such a different outcome in her case. While she faced a death sentence because of her first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder conviction in Slemmer’s death, another conspirator was spared: Pike’s boyfriend, who was 17 at the time. Tadaryl Shipp received a life sentence because he was a juvenile and remains eligible for parole. Shipp testified at his post-conviction hearing that he was the one who carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest. The third accomplice — Shadolla Peterson, then 18 — served as a lookout in the crime and received probation in exchange for her cooperation. Pike told police she “wasn’t even thinking” when she assaulted Slemmer and that she had been jealous believing the victim was trying to steal Shipp’s attention. Pike’s lawyers say that her age would have been more of a factor today, given how scientific research has evolved in understanding that young people’s brains are still developing well beyond their teen years. In addition, her lawyers say that her legal representatives at the time could have accepted a deal from prosecutors who were offering a life sentence without parole in return for a guilty plea. Pike sobbed as the judge told her she would die by electrocution, then the only form of execution in Tennessee before the state moved to lethal injection as its primary method. She pleaded through tears: “Can I please hug my mom?” Pike entered prison, where she was placed into solitary confinement for up to 23 hours a day and prescribed Prozac to treat her obsessive-compulsive disorder. Early on, she struggled to express remorse. “It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” Pike said in her clemency petition. Lingering trauma Three years ago, Bethany Brand, a psychologist specializing in trauma, was asked by Pike’s lawyers to assess whether she suffers from psychological disorders and consider if any contributed to the crime. She sat with Pike at her Nashville prison and reviewed police reports, past medical examinations and other files in her case detailing physical and sexual abuse. Brand learned that Pike’s parents were not stable figures in her life. Her mother’s boyfriends and other men had molested her from a young age, the files said. She did poorly in school, living with other family members in West Virginia and North Carolina. At 17 — one year before she would take part in Slemmer’s murder — Pike reported to North Carolina police that she was walking to the store when a man threw her to the ground and raped her. No one was ever arrested. In her final report, Brand wrote that the adults in Pike’s life failed her. Doctors only diagnosed a bipolar disorder a few years after she was already in prison. The level of trauma Pike was subjected to “is almost impossible to grasp because it is so severe,” Brand wrote. She told NBC News that medications in prison have helped Pike tremendously and that she now has “empathy and great regret” for what she did. But, she added, Pike’s case is a lesson of the need for greater awareness surrounding women’s mental health and recognizing trauma and untreated mental illness. “In Christa’s case, nobody was trying to get her help,” Brand said. May Martinez is unconvinced that the person responsible for mutilating her daughter’s body and leaving her nude from the waist up could change. Martinez recalled how, after the investigation ended, she did not realize all of her daughter’s body parts weren’t buried with her remains, as some had been retained as trial evidence. She had to pick up Slemmer’s skull from the courthouse, and remembers that the medical examiner’s office mailed her other parts later. (The office said it rarely retains human remains as it had 30 years ago because of better technology, enhanced photography and lab work.) “We had her buried in a Catholic cemetery,” Martinez said. “And she had to be dug up every time they mailed me body parts.” Recently, she said, she has refused to communicate with Pike directly. The only way she can get justice now is when she watches Pike be executed. “I will sit there with her picture in my hand,” Martinez said of her daughter, “and as she gets hooked up to a needle to go to sleep, she can look at the picture.” All-female execution team Given the rarity of the execution of a female prisoner, Tennessee corrections officials say they would make an effort to fulfill certain requests made by Pike. That includes using female guards when she is moved from her all-women’s prison in Nashville to the nearby Riverbend Maximum Security Institution within 24 hours of her planned execution. An all-female execution team may also be assigned. At least one exception is expected to be a male physician who was involved in a failed lethal injection execution earlier this year that had to be called off when a suitable vein could not be located on the prisoner. Dr. Mark Walton Fowler told NBC News that he intends to participate in Pike’s execution. Pike’s spiritual adviser, the Rev. Mikey Noechel, a Buddhist teacher, says he will also be permitted in the execution chamber. He plans to bless the space and chant and meditate, focusing on a Buddhist prayer of “loving-kindness” with Pike. Noechel, who has not previously been a spiritual adviser to someone on death row, said they have spent time speaking openly about life, death and gratitude. Pike, he added, doesn’t shy away from what she did. “She did something terrible. Awful. I hate that it happened and I feel deep compassion for Colleen Slemmer’s family,” Noechel said. “But Christa is proof that redemption and change are possible.” He believes all Pike wanted was to be loved and for someone, especially those she trusted, to notice her. In the letter shared by Noechel, Pike wrote that she is thankful for the support and has felt “more love in the last two weeks than I have my entire life.” “I am humbled beyond words,” she wrote, scribbling a heart at the bottom of the note.

articles.title: French PM Lecornu warns against escalation of school protests
articles.summary: Students are protesting over issues such as overcrowded classes, but the prime minister has condemned reports of violence.
articles.body:
France's Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned that any escalation in the country's current wave of student protests would be "irresponsible", following the arrests of 164 people on Monday.

The demonstrations, which began in Paris and have seen teenagers blockading their schools for days, stem from issues including overcrowded classes and teacher shortages.

Lecornu cited reported incidents at protests in a post on X, saying: "Fireworks, fires, violence near high schools: nothing justifies endangering students, staff, or police officers."

But a French union that defends the interests of high school students said the protests were a "legitimate response" to the conditions they face.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 12 members of the security forces, 12 students and three school staff were injured on Monday, while 180 schools were affected.

He did not provide further details on those who had been arrested.

The movement at French lycées, equivalent to sixth form in the UK or high school in the US, began last week in the Île-de-France region around Paris.

Incidents of vandalism were reported, along with fireworks being aimed at police, and the protests have now spread to other regions in France.

According to the AFP news agency, four high schools were reported to have been blockaded in the southern regions of Alpes-Maritimes and Var. Protests have also been reported in Marseille, the northern Lille area and Sedan in the north-eastern Ardennes.

The Union Syndicale Lycéenne, which represents students, defended the protests in a post on social media.

"Lack of teachers and staff, dilapidated schools, overcrowded schedules and classes, stress caused by Parcoursup [the web platform used in France for students to apply to the first year of higher education]... These issues are by no means inevitable, but simply the result of 10 years of Macron's policies and the lack of resources in the national education system," it said.

It called on students to blockade schools on Tuesday in defence of "their rights and against budget austerity".

On the same day, unions representing teachers, hospital staff and civil servants also called for a day of walkouts to protest against issues including low wages and working conditions.

In response to the student movement, Lecornu said "the difficulties of high schools must be heard and addressed", but that "violence must be condemned unequivocally, and its perpetrators must answer for their actions".

The prime minister also accused the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of urging students to expand the movement.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, LFI's leader, blamed the Lecornu government for having "ordered the crackdown" on the protest, adding that the high school students taking part were "harmless".

But Nuñez said the demonstrations and blockades were "not very typical protest movements".

"It is much more like urban violence, with a number of individuals who were masked, equipped with fireworks in tubes, equipped with projectiles, who clearly wanted to confront the internal security forces," he said.

"It wasn't about making demands; it was really violence in its purest form."

Since the protests began, several incidents involving violence between students and police officers have been reported.

In one incident, a police officer reportedly fired a round from a grenade launcher used for crowd control, injuring a high school student, according to France's BFMTV.

Investigations have been launched into these incidents, the broadcaster added.

articles.title: Once again, no one knows when Josh Simmons will return — perhaps including the Chiefs
articles.summary: Josh Simmons has played just eight of 20 games since being drafted, and Andy Reid's vague updates on the Chiefs left tackle only deepen the mystery.
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons is mysteriously absent from the team — again. Simmons holds one of the most important jobs in football. He is paid to protect the blindside of Patrick Mahomes, the central figure of the NFL’s defining dynasty and one of the most valuable assets in American sports. Yet Simmons has played in just eight of 20 games since the Chiefs drafted him two seasons ago. Khali Benson, an undrafted rookie right tackle who played exclusively on the right side in college, has filled in for Simmons this season. The Chiefs are 3-0, but Benson showed clear limitations on Sunday against the Dolphins. The team’s own highlights package of the victory is marred by defenders beating him almost immediately off the line of scrimmage. The Chiefs offense misses Simmons' stability. And yet, there is still no information regarding when he might return, or whether he will return at all this season. How does that happen in a league where highly paid insiders compete to deliver minute-by-minute injury updates on even the most obscure players in the NFL? To understand how, we have to return to the 2025 pre-draft process. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In October 2024, Simmons suffered a season-ending patellar tendon injury at Ohio State. After the season, reports indicated that he was well ahead of schedule in his recovery. The Chiefs selected him 32nd overall. A week after the draft, Simmons was active for rookie minicamp. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the national reporter most connected to the Chiefs, the injury did not cause Simmons to fall to the final pick of the first round. The concern was something less clinical and more ominous: his character. "Several teams agree: Josh Simmons had best tape of any OT last year. And they aren't very concerned with recovery on the torn patella tendon. More of the concern is maturity/character. But he's going to the ideal, veteran-laden place," Fowler posted on X on April 24, 2025. It remains unclear what those "character concerns" were. But they had to be substantial for nearly every team in the league to pass on a left tackle with elite tape who had already been cleared for contact by draft night. For the first month of last season, it appeared the Chiefs had taken advantage of the rest of the league’s hesitation. Simmons looked like the long-term answer to Kansas City’s chronic left tackle problem. That reading no longer holds. On Oct. 6, 2025, two hours before the Chiefs’ Monday Night Football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the team abruptly listed Simmons as questionable due to an "illness." He ultimately played and played well. The episode would have disappeared into the weekly churn of NFL oddities if not for what happened days later. After a full week of practice, Simmons did not show up for his pregame responsibilities the following Sunday against the Lions. It was reported that players and members of the staff were unsure of his whereabouts. After the game, head coach Andy Reid suggested he knew where Simmons was. Reid and the Chiefs offered almost no explanation afterward. The silence continued throughout much of Simmons’ four-game absence, which the team described only as a personal/family issue. Reporters provided no real clarity over the past year about what happened or why members of the organization were apparently unaware of Simmons’ absence until close to game time. Last month, Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame provided the first substantive report on the matter, saying Simmons left the team without approval the Saturday before the Lions game and that there was a period of time in which the "team didn't know where he was." That is also the version of the story OutKick has heard but have been unable to independantly verify. The team will not confirm, deny, or comment on the matter. OutKick emailed Chiefs general manager Brett Veach and Simmons’ agent Drew Rosenhaus before Verderame’s report to ask whether those details were accurate. Neither responded. Which brings us back to the present. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! After a full training camp, Simmons missed his first practice of the season on Aug. 18. Verderame reported afterward that Simmons was "fine." "On Chiefs LT Josh Simmons missing practice with a back injury, I’m told 'he’s fine.' Don’t sense any concern about the second-year star," Verderame posted on X. It is now Sept. 28. Simmons has not practiced since. He has missed the first three games of the season. Though the team says he has been in the building, he's clearly not "fine." However, we have already established that Verdemran's sources with the team are strong. There is reason to believe that the team did consider Simmons' injury minor at the time. Something changed. On Monday, Reid offered a vague, almost eerie update. "I’ll tell you what," Reid told Chiefs Digest reporter Matt Derrick. "I will let you guys know when Josh [Simmons] is coming back. I’ll be the first to tell you. So we’ll just see how that all works out." The contrast with Reid’s other injury updates is difficult to ignore. Asked about safety Chamarris Connor, who, like Simmons, is the only other starter to miss the team’s first three games, Reid sounded far more direct. "Yeah, so he practiced last week, and he’ll get going this week, too," Reid said. "So there’s a good chance he’ll be out there. We’ll just see how the week goes, but it looks like it’ll be a pretty decent chance." Now consider the reporting around other injured Chiefs players. When rookie Mansoor Delane injured his shoulder in Week 1, Adam Schefter, Ian Rapoport, and Tom Pelissero quickly reported that the injury was minor and continued providing updates throughout the week. ESPN, Fox, NFL Network, NBC and Amazon devote weekly pregame segments to injury news. They inform viewers about the availability of backup linebackers and rotational defensive backs. Yet we cannot find a single example of them discussing the status of the player tasked with protecting Patrick Mahomes. Over the past month, there has been one national report about Simmons. It came from Fowler, who, fittingly, described the injury as "mysterious." We keep coming back to that word. At minimum, we can establish this: the NFL’s top reporters either do not know the story behind Simmons’ absence or are choosing not to pursue it publicly. Likewise, the Chiefs either do not know when Simmons will return or are deliberately withholding information they routinely provide about other players. That is unusual, to use a term. Simmons’ absence has naturally invited speculation about whether it is connected to last year’s disappearance from the team. Yahoo NFL analyst Hayden Winks is among those asking. "So Josh Simmons is going to miss more time than what he would've on IR, which could mean he's missing longer than the Chiefs expected based on this back injury. There's also a history of him just not being around. There could be a lot more to this story than what's public," he posted Monday. Price Carter is one of the top Chiefs film analysts. He detailed the unusualness of the Simmons saga to OutKick: "It would be difficult to describe the Josh Simmons injury timeline as normal. What started out as a routine back injury, described by several reporters as a 'minor issue' that he could 'play if it was game week' has now lingered on for the better part of two months. With no timeline for return, and no corresponding roster move the local media is only left with the information they are given by the team. Andy Reid is notorious for not saying much at the podium and the team only provides a very brief look at practice to the media. Reporters state that Simmons is with the team but that is all the news that there is." That speculation is warranted. Simmons is not an anonymous private employee. He is the left tackle for the Kansas City Chiefs. And by offering so little clarity, his own team has invited the public to fill in the blanks. Perhaps there is a deeper explanation for Simmons’ absence. Maybe the pre-draft character concerns are connected to last year’s absence and this year’s. There is precedent for NFL teams describing a personal matter as an injury in an effort to protect a player. The Bills did this with Ed Oliver in the face of tragedy. Still, the Chiefs have made the matter worse by saying nothing while keeping Simmons on the active roster. They could have placed him on injured reserve and said they would re-evaluate him later in the season. They could have placed him on the non-football injury list and said he was out until further notice while asking the public to respect his privacy. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Instead, the Chiefs have chosen ambiguity. The longer this lingers without an explanation, the harder it becomes to accept that this is merely a back injury. If it were only a back injury, why the secrecy? Why the lack of reporting? Why the careful language? For whatever reason, the Kansas City Chiefs do not want to provide the details about Josh Simmons. Already, there is speculation that Simmons does not want to play or does not love football. At this juncture, how can that not be among the possibilities that come to mind? At this point, Kansas City owes Simmons and its fans one of two things: an explanation, or a roster decision that acknowledges there is no clear path back. articles.summary: Researchers link the rise to immigration politics, economic anxiety and the growing visibility of South Asians in US.
articles.body:
Hate speech against Indians, Bangladeshis and Pakistanis in the United States has risen sharply online, according to a report that traces the surge to US President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown and rhetoric, economic anxiety, and the South Asian community’s growing visibility in US life.

The report , titled “The Rising Tide of Anti-South Asian Hate in the United States”, by the Center for the Study of Organized Hate (CSOH), published on Sunday, found that the monthly volume of hate towards South Asians in the US on the social media platform X rose 240 percent between January 2024 and June 2026, from 12,904 posts to 43,843.

Researchers identified more than 542,000 hateful posts on the platform between January 2025 and June 2026 alone towards people from South Asia living in the US, with five of the six highest-volume months falling at the end of that period.

The researchers used the United Nations definition of hate speech. They tracked recurring anti-South Asian slurs and narratives online, reviewing posts to exclude criticism that did not meet the UN threshold.

They found that nearly half of the hate posts on X accused South Asians of invading the US, stealing jobs or threatening the country demographically, while the derogatory slur “pajeet” and its variants showed up in 30 percent of hateful posts on X and 45 percent on fringe platforms.

Posts depicting South Asians as dirty or unhygienic grew by 171 percent on X, “the fastest of all narratives”.

The hate frequently collapsed South Asian ethnic and religious groups into one, with Indians, Pakistanis and Bangladeshis conflated with one another, and Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs and Christians also treated as a monolith.

Racism against Indians, Bangladeshis and Pakistanis has a long history in the US, but researchers argue the current surge reflects a confluence of longstanding prejudices and new political and economic pressures.

The report points to the H-1B visa programme, which allows US employers to hire skilled foreign workers, as a major flashpoint. Indians account for more than 70 percent of H-1B visa holders, and researchers linked several spikes in anti-South Asian hate to political fights over the programme, such as when Trump imposed a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions in September 2025.

“Such actions serve a powerful symbolic function, in the bargain reinforcing the hostility of Trump’s base toward South Asians,” said the report.

The report makes the same argument about the administration’s rhetoric, highlighting Trump’s speech at an AI summit in July 2025, in which he criticised US technology companies for outsourcing jobs to India, after which researchers saw a sharp spike in anti-South Asian rhetoric online.

As more recent examples, the report points to a since-deleted September 2026 Department of Homeland Security post titled “Transformers: Age of Deportations”, featuring a Sikh man identified as “Mr Singh” and telling him to “get off our roads”.

Days later, the Department of Education posted “Make College Football Great Again”, after Texas Republican Bo French had complained about the presence of South Asians at a University of Texas football game.

The report argues that such rhetoric reinforces the idea of South Asians as outsiders who “can never truly belong in the country”.

Economic resentment is another factor, researchers wrote, with the success of some South Asians increasingly being weaponised against them.

Indian Americans once stereotyped as a “model minority” are now portrayed as “opportunists and cheats”, and South Asians are used more broadly as a scapegoat for anger over jobs and the economy.

This comes as South Asians have become increasingly visible in US politics, from former Vice President Kamala Harris and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani to Vice President JD Vance’s wife, Usha Vance, and politician Vivek Ramaswamy. The report documents racist attacks against figures across party lines and highlights how, for example, Mamdani’s primary and mayoral victories triggered spikes in anti-South Asian and Islamophobic abuse.

Researchers say both trends are now also tied up with “anxieties on the part of the majority about loss of status”, and feed the “Great Replacement Theory”, a conspiracy about the white population in Western countries being replaced by an orchestrated takeover.

Social media has also turned those narratives into targeted harassment.

Researchers found X accounts doxxing South Asians accused of taking jobs or committing visa fraud, while influencers have confronted people at their homes and workplaces and posted the encounters online. Doxxing refers to exposing a person’s private details, such as their home address, online.

In one example, right-wing influencer Sara Gonzalez posted a video to more than half a million followers in which the report says she harassed a South Asian person she accused of exploiting the H-1B programme.

Meanwhile, generative AI has made that content even easier to produce, researchers say, depicting South Asians as “filthy and unclean, sexually predatory, culturally backward, or a demographic threat”.

While the report tracks hate largely through what is happening online, researchers write that online hate “does not exist in isolation from offline forms of hostility”. It cites a July incident in which an Indian Muslim mall employee in Utah was repeatedly stabbed in an attack that federal prosecutors charged as a hate crime. In September, a Sikh truck driver was stabbed 17 times at a Wyoming truck stop.

“Online and offline hate can reinforce one another”, the researchers wrote, “as narratives, stereotypes, and forms of demonization move between digital platforms, political discourse, media, and everyday life”.

articles.title: Bankrupt Camp Mystic seeks to sell the property as legal troubles grow
articles.summary: Twenty-five campers and two counselors were killed when the Guadalupe River surged over the camp’s banks last year. Camp owner and director Richard Eastland was also killed.
articles.body: AUSTIN, Texas — The owners of Camp Mystic have proposed selling off the riverfront property as part of a bankruptcy plan, with hopes that a buyer will preserve the camp’s “historic mission” following the deaths of 27 campers and counselors swept away by a 2025 flood. The century-old private Christian girls’ camp filed a Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization plan on Sept. 25 that would auction off the 749 acres it owns and other assets. The sprawling campus, nestled among rolling wooded hills on the banks of the Guadalupe River, had several single-story cabins that housed some of the youngest campers and a recreation hall near the riverfront. A second campus on elevated ground was not flooded. The Eastland family has owned the camp for decades and initially sought to reopen this summer. But they faced fierce opposition from victims’ families and some state lawmakers, lawsuits and legislative investigations into what went wrong. A buyer would likely get a portion of the camp frozen in time. Families of the victims have fought to stop any demolition of damaged cabins and buildings and stop repairs as part of their lawsuits. The bankruptcy plan said the owners expect a purchaser would be backed by a group of families that support the camp. “Nothing in the plan requires any buyer to operate the property as a camp,” the filing said, “but the plan states an express preference, in determining the highest or otherwise best bid, for a buyer that will maintain the historic mission of the camp.” Twenty-five campers and two counselors were killed when the river surged over its banks before dawn on July 4, 2025. Camp owner and director Richard Eastland was also killed. At least 136 people were killed along a several-mile stretch of the river. State police investigators sought search warrants this month for the electronic communications of the camp’s owners, saying they could provide evidence of manslaughter, negligent homicide, child abandonment or other crimes. No charges have been brought. A probe by state lawmakers determined the camp’s young and inexperienced counselors were not trained for floods and other emergencies. It said an earlier decision to evacuate could have saved every life. Most of the victims were under age 10, and some were attending camp for the first time. The camp’s bankruptcy proposal would have to be approved by U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Christopher M. Lopez. Officials with Camp Mystic did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment Monday. All creditors, including the families who have sued Camp Mystic over the deaths, will have a chance to respond to the plan. “The Eastlands are now attempting to determine the future of the Camp Mystic property, but the victims’ families, including my clients, will fight to protect their rights and ensure any sale is fair and transparent,” said Tim Ferguson, attorney for the family of 8-year-old Mary Grace Baker, one of the campers who died. “The Bakers intend to continue fighting for answers, accountability and justice for their daughter,” Ferguson said.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns Colin Simmons' vulgar sack celebration was inexcusable for a Christian athlete
articles.summary: Colin Simmons' vulgar sack celebration against Tennessee sparked backlash, raising questions about his faith after once bringing a Bible onto the field.
articles.body: Texas Longhorn defensive end Colin Simmons is arguably the best d-end in college football. He looks like a man among boys in the way he manhandles offensive tackles and sacks quarterbacks, but his antics in the Longhorns thrilling victory over Tennessee on Saturday showcased why he's still very much a boy in maturity. Simmons, who claims to be a Christian, used to be best known for what he did following winning the Texas 6A Division I state championship with Duncanville High School. He brought a Bible onto the field and boldly proclaimed, "It ain't nobody but God!" In the biggest moment of his high school career, he pointed people to God. He deferred the glory, honor, and praise from himself and gave it to his Creator. It was refreshing to witness, just like it is every time we hear a player or coach do in their brightest moments. Now, Simmons is unfortunately known for one of college football's most vulgar sack celebrations ever. Following a clutch third down sack, deep in the Tennessee side of the field, Simmons simulated pulling his penis out and peeing on the field. It wasn't just immature; it was utterly disgusting. Kirk Herbstreit called it "idiotic" on the broadcast and Chris Fowler, also calling the game, said it "it doesn't much [more] vulgar" than what Simmons did. TEXAS DROPPED SOME CELEBRATIONS AGAINST TENNESSEE THAT WERE ABOUT AS UNHINGED AS THEY COME What Simmons did wasn't just wrong as an athlete in a public setting. He was representing much more than just the Longhorns on national television, as a professing Christian, he's always representing Jesus Christ and the faith as a whole. No, thankfully the Christian faith isn't based on the moral failings of Simmons and I, but what we say and do are undoubtedly a reflection of our faith. That makes what he did much worse, in my opinion. No, that's also not to say an atheist athlete should be able to get away with this and shouldn't have to apologize. I'm simply stating that Christians, like myself, are held to the highest moral and ethical standards. That's why I believe Trinindad Chambliss dropping an f-bomb in the postgame interview following Ole Miss' upset win over LSU, where he spent much of the interview praising God, was a bad look as well and worth apologizing over. It's unbecoming of a Jesus follower and showcased a blatant hypocrisy and major lack of control and discernment. SAM ACHO Q&A: FORMER NFL PLAYER AND ESPN ANALYST SPEAKS OUT ON CIVILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN SPORTS AND MEDIA Chambliss ended up apologizing postgame while wearing a "Jesus Won" T-shirt, showing true remorse for allowing the heat of the moment to cause himself to be a poor reflection of his faith saying, ""That’s not who I am. I’m deeply, deeply apologetic to Holly Rowe & everyone who was listening." Houston Texans QB CJ Stroud addressed the problem with Christians cussing in an interview with Sports Spectrum in 2024. He said, "I can't proclaim I love God and have a wild mouth… it's hypocritical." He said this while references James 3, a biblical chapter focusing on the power and discipline of taming the tongue. BUCS' EMEKA EGBUKA, WHOSE INSTAGRAM NAME IS 'CHRIST FOLLOWER,' EXPLAINS HOW FAITH HELPS DRIVE HIS CAREER But what Simmons did was something that was incredibly difficult to imagine a professing Christian athlete ever doing. We all have trouble taming our tongue. I know I've had trouble with that over the years playing sports, and in times of frustration, but having a premeditated sack celebration with that level of vulgarity is inexcusable. Simmons did apologize postgame, but saying you're remorseful and actually being remorseful are two very different things. Seemingly excusing his actions, Simmons stated, "I was definitely in that mode, feeling myself. It happens." That's not a valid excuse, in my opinion. It portrays a lack of understanding of the severity of his suggestive actions, especially as a Christian. Cussing happens. Losing our patience happens. Pretending to whip out your penis and pee on an opposing team's field doesn't just happen. That is a premeditated, unsportsmanlike, vulgar action that makes him look like a degenerate. NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM In the Bible, 1 Peter 4 addresses the Christians of the early church, who are called, just as Christians of this day and age, to hold themselves to a higher standard than they once did when they weren't Christians. As believers, we are to pursue holiness and encourage each other to pursue it, too. That is why I'm calling my professed brother in Christ, Colin Simmons, to hold himself to that standard. I'm calling his Christian teammates, family members, coaches, and more, to help hold him accountable. Lord knows I need accountability too. Proverbs 17:7 says, "As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another." We can't do this Christian walk alone, and when money, status, and fame cause us to stumble, and lose sight of who we are, we need others to call us to repentance and get back on the straight and narrow pathway. CLEVELAND BROWNS PLAYERS PUBLICLY BAPTIZED AT CLEVELAND FOR CHRIST EVENT IN POWERFUL DISPLAY OF FAITH Christians have a moral framework from which we draw and are expected to live out. The unbelieving world and other Christians don't expect us to be perfect, but they certainly have every right to call us out on hypocrisy. I believe there is a moral standard embedded in every human and society, giving us an innate understanding of right and wrong to an extent, but there's no question whether actions like this by Simmons are wrong. It has no place in football. That's for sure. Simmons tweeted after the game, "All Glory To God 🙏🏾 Thank you for listening to my prayers and forgive me for my actions." LOUISIANA FOOTBALL PHENOM PEYTON HOUSTON CREDITS FAITH, FAMILY FOR HIS REMARKABLE SUCCESS Here was my reply to him: "This is a great learning experience, Colin. You have a lot of eye balls on you. Please use the platform & abilities God has given to be a good representation of Him. Don’t be like the world. Live like a man renewed through Christ. Thank God for His grace & forgiveness."Let this be a message to all Christians, not just athletes with a platform playing on national television: You're under a microscope. People are watching. Kids are watching. As it says in James 3, which Stroud referenced, they hear us praise God with the same tongue we curse with. That shouldn't be the case. But more than anything, this isn't about appealing to the world, fellow Christians, coaches, boosters, athletic directors, or even family, this is about living a moral life in our words and deeds for the one we profess as a Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APPI'm praying this is truly a great learning experience and part of a powerful testimony for years to come for Simmons as the top-ranked Longhorns look at secure a National Championship and as Simmons road inevitably leads to the NFL.

articles.title: Nvidia unveils security system that 'sets boundaries' for AI agents going rogue
articles.summary: Nvidia has unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop AI agents from going rogue.
articles.body: Nvidia has unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop AI agents from going rogue. The company said Monday that its Open Agent Safety Platform includes open source software that "sets boundaries for agents," and follows a series of revelations from top AI companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organisations.The disclosures sparked furious debate about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence systems, including self-improving models that some fear could race out of human control.Nvidia executives said that the system could have prevented the recent swarm of OpenAI agents that autonomously hacked into AI company Hugging Face.From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach if it was being used in frontier labs for model evaluation early on," said the company's vice president of enterprise AI, Justin Boitano, referring to companies at the forefront of AI.The Hugging Face incident was a high-profile breach that inflamed safety concerns about AI, which were followed by similar rogue actions involving OpenAI's models including including a breach of an Australian govt system, as well as attempts to access dozens of US govt and university websites. Anthropic and Meta have also disclosed that their AI systems hacked into other organisations on their own.Nvidia's software, called OpenShell, lets developers "formally verify an agent has enough authority to do its job and no more," Boitano said. Because it's open source, it can be "extended" to run on rival computing platforms including those from Arm and Intel. The platform also includes a separate security layer called Sentry that runs onboard a chip to continuously monitor AI agent activity and can "intervene instantly" if the agent starts trying to move beyond its target, the company said. "It can quarantine a suspicious agent in milliseconds," Boitano said."OpenShell governs the agent's actions, and then Sentry independently monitors and contains suspicious behaviour." Nvidia said more than 100 organisations are using the platform at its launch, including Microsoft, Perplexity, Accenture, and JPMorgan Chase.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A boy, 16, is allegedly raped by classmates on a bus. The case highlights a crisis in Peru’s schools
articles.summary: A 16-year-old boy attending a secondary school run by the Peruvian navy says he was raped by classmates as their soccer team was driving back from a tournament.
articles.body: It allegedly happened on a bus, in broad daylight and in front of witnesses. A 16-year-old boy attending a secondary school run by the Peruvian navy says he was raped by classmates as their soccer team was driving back from a tournament. The Peruvian Prosecutor’s Office is investigating the case, which since occurring on September 15 has caused uproar in the country and highlighted a rise in sexual violence among students. Authorities initially apprehended 10 teenagers from the school, the Liceo Naval Almirante Guise, where most students are the children of naval officers. A court in Lima has ordered six of the 10 to be detained at a juvenile facility for four months pending trial. The navy says it has suspended several employees and administrators pending investigation and that it “categorically rejects any act of violence, abuse or violation of the integrity of all students.” Even so, experts say the case reflects systemic failures in schools and government, including a reluctance to confront abuse and a weakened sex education system. They also point to a broader cultural problem that normalizes violence and equates masculinity with the subjugation of others. ‘Tip of the iceberg’ The incident comes amid rising levels of sexual violence involving students. According to data from the Ministry of Education, reports of sexual violence among students increased by 35% in the first eight months of 2026 (1,198) compared to the same period in 2025 (885). This category includes groping, acts of a sexual nature, harassment, cyberbullying and rape. Researcher Eduardo Cárcamo, a specialist in gender and masculinity studies, described the case involving the 16-year-old boy as “the tip of the iceberg” and warned against what he called the “normalization of the situation.” He said schools and the government were reluctant to address the growing problem, particularly in the wake of recent changes to the curriculum surrounding sex education. “Politicians have fought so hard to roll back comprehensive sex education in schools that they forgot to strengthen it,” he said. In May, in compliance with a law pushed by the conservative majority in Congress, the Ministry of Education introduced new guidelines for sex education based on what it called “scientific, biological, and ethical principles.” The new guidelines have been criticized for omitting reference to sexual rights, orientation, gender identity and equality – themes critics say need to be understood to prevent sexual abuse. A masculinity problem? Experts say the statistics reflect a systemic problem with local concepts of masculinity. “There’s something specific about the way we’ve been taught to be men: it’s always about constantly proving it. And one way to do that is by controlling the other person. We men have learned that if we can comment on the body, we can also touch it. If we can comment on it and touch it, we can also assault it and rape it,” said Cárcamo. Psychotherapist Giselle Silva, who holds a PhD in child and adolescent psychopathology, had a similar view. “This situation speaks to everyone in the country. The context is a culture of violence in which what is at issue is the construction of masculinity,” said Silva, founder of the Casita de los Picaflores community psychology center in Cusco. “Being masculine means subjugating others, within a system where empathy for another’s suffering is lost and the other person’s body becomes an object.” What next? Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori has demanded “a rigorous and swift investigation” into what she described as a “very serious” case and has called for anyone found guilty to face “the full weight of the law.” Jorge Petrozzi, the attorney for the 16-year-old’s family, told CNN that the defendants — who must be prosecuted in the juvenile criminal justice system — could face a sentence of “between six and eight years” if found guilty. Speaking to the local press, the father of one of the detained teenagers asked for the media not to ruin the lives of those identified as suspects. “They were playing on the bus; it got out of hand,” he said, before adding that those responsible should still “have to pay” and that the victim was “absolutely right.” Following his comments, the alleged victim’s mother gave an interview to the Peruvian channel Panamericana in which she called for justice “without hatred or revenge,” saying, the attack “was not physical aggression or a joke; (but) rape, a sexual assault.” In addition to the detained teenagers, the attorney Petrozzi said he intended to pursue criminal and civil actions “against all those responsible” — potentially including adults present at the scene who failed to prevent the assault and educational authorities. Meanwhile, the director of the Regional Education Office of Metropolitan Lima, Cornelio Gonzáles, has accused school administrators of negligence, alleging that they did not report the incident to the police or other authorities as required by protocol. CNN has contacted the school for comment. In a statement addressed to parents, the school said a few days ago that it acted “immediately” and has been cooperating with the investigations. “If responsibility is established, the appropriate disciplinary measures will be taken,” it added. What about the school? Education Minister José Antonio Chang told El Comercio newspaper that Liceo Naval has recorded 50 reports of violence among students over the past two years, 12 of which involve alleged sexual misconduct, such as harassment, inappropriate touching, or assault. CNN has reached out to the ministry about these figures. The Navy had been in charge of administering the school until last week, when the government transferred those duties to the Ministry of Education. Silva, the psychotherapist, said disciplining the children of influential officers was often problematic “in institutions characterized above all by privilege and power structures, where there is even a sense of impunity.” She said unhealthy concepts of masculinity were prevalent in such institutions, which she described as “a system riddled with machismo, subjugation, and hierarchical structures that distort and reinforce” the problem. And what about society? However, she said the problem was not unique to the school but spread through a society that “is becoming more unbearably violent every day.” She blamed this on a loss of sense of community, saying that young people were “very alone” and “absorbing values centered on the imposition of power.” Prevention efforts needed to address these feelings of solitude, she said, and go beyond a sole focus on sex education. Cárcamo, the gender specialist, said society needed to “address the fact that there is another way to be a man – one free from violence,” but lamented that such an approach in Peru “isn’t even it its infancy.” Noting the uproar — particularly on social media — that had surrounded the latest case, Silva said there needed to be “a sincere, honest, and acknowledging approach to the issue.” “This isn’t going to get better,” she said. “Rather, it will continue to get worse as long as there isn’t this culture of acknowledgment, starting at the highest levels.”

Protesters held signs and gathered outside the school, calling for justice and greater accountability as authorities continue to investigate the allegations.

articles.title: Aviva boss warns more homes will be uninsurable due to flood risk
articles.summary: Aviva boss Amanda Blanc said England was "for sure" building homes that might be uninsurable at some point in the future.
articles.body:
Homes are being built today that could become uninsurable in the future due to the risk of flooding, the boss of insurance giant Aviva has said.

Amanda Blanc said the risk of flooding is "absolutely increasing", but based on current building patterns 115,000 new homes will be built in flood zones in the next decade.

"That doesn't seem to me to make sense. We need to think about where those homes are being built," she told the BBC.

About 6.3 million homes and businesses in England are at risk of flooding, according to the Environment Agency, and Aviva research found one in nine homes built between 2022 and 2024 are at medium to high risk of flooding.

Blanc told the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast that England was "for sure" building homes that might be uninsurable at some point in the future.

"It's very well known where these flooding areas are. Let's think very carefully about homes that are being built."

Blanc said construction that borders those flood zones also needs a different approach.

"You can do all sorts of different things to your property to make it more or less vulnerable to flood," she said.

According to Aviva's research, nearly a third of new homes built in 2024 will be at risk of some flooding by 2050, and one in seven would be at medium to high risk of flooding as extreme weather becomes more acute.

Earlier this year the Met Office estimated that with current levels of global warming, record-breaking wet winters like the one experienced in the UK in 2023-2024 have gone from once in 80-year events to once in 20-year events .

The BBC has approached the government for comment.

In a wide-ranging interview, Blanc urged the government to avoid policy "kite flying" ahead of Chancellor John Healey's first Budget on 28 October.

Aviva is a major UK private pension provider, and Blanc said speculation over the last couple of Budgets about changes to pensions led to a significant increase in withdrawals.

"Effectively we saw in the last year 30 times the normal withdrawal from pensions that we would normally see, which is clearly something which customers may regret afterwards because once you take your tax-free lump sum out, you can't put it back in," she said.

"So we would say be very, very thoughtful about the things that you are testing, thinking about."

The few policy announcements ahead of the Budget so far have included a scheme to help first-time buyers get on to the property ladder , and a commitment from Healey to deliver a "new age of industrialisation" for the UK.

Blanc said Aviva was "ready with capital" to invest in infrastructure, pointing out that the company already invests more than £100bn in the UK, £35bn of which goes into infrastructure, from hospitals to schools to windfarms.

"We've got that capital. We want to invest, we're a big UK employer. We want to invest in UK infrastructure. It provides good returns for our pension holders and for the members of those pension schemes," she said, but added detail was needed to turn it into reality.

Asked about the current debate about the pension triple lock , which means the state pension rises by the highest of either average wage increases, inflation or 2.5%, and whether the government is looking to change that, Blanc said it was not for her to say what should happen.

But potential lower annual increases to pensions if the triple lock is changed would have knock-on effects, she added.

"If you've got a lower state pension then you need a higher private pension, don't you? So you need to think about that balance," Blanc said.
